chunks: And in the narration of Durust ibn Abī Manṣūr, he said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:
Concerning zakat, a man sends it to a town other than his own. So he said: “There is no harm; he may send one-third or one-fourth.”

key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms-tax under discussion here
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to send part of one's zakat to another town?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the transfer of zakat to a place other than one's own locality. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that there is no harm in sending a portion of it, such as one-third or one-fourth, indicating permissibility in distributing part of zakat beyond one’s own town.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1620 - In a narration from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, it is reported that Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said regarding Zakat:
"A man may send a portion of his Zakat to a place other than his own. He said, 'There is no issue if he sends one-third or one-fourth of it.'"
